analysis.title: Monthly Hedge Fund Performance Review, October 2026
key_insights: Asset-weighted HF Composite returned -1.25% in October 2026, with 3-month return -0.57% and YTD +6.87%.
Equity L/S was the weakest master strategy at -2.64% (3M -3.08%, YTD +7.58%), with losses across all sub-strategies. Asia Pacific L/S fell most at -5.37%.
Event driven declined least at -0.24%, YTD +4.49%.
The AI spending sell-off drove the month. Concerns over returns on AI capex hit US and Asian tech and semiconductor shares, intensifying toward month-end after US earnings.
Long biased returned -0.57%. Diversified growth led at +1.45%, long biased other was weakest at -6.80%. UK equities helped via energy strength.
Quant returned -0.75% after a sharp factor rotation from tech to value and defensives. Risk premia (+0.30%) was the only positive sub-strategy, quant multi-strategy funds fell -1.55%.
Multi-strategy returned -1.47%. Largest funds (AUM above US$10bn) fell -1.36%, smallest (below US$0.5bn) fell -2.44%. De-grossing and unwinds of crowded AI and tech trades drove losses.

Macro returned -1.52%. Commodities macro (+0.82%) was the only positive sub-strategy, global macro (-2.35%) weakest on flattening curves and shifting rate expectations. EM macro was hit by Brazil's surprise election result.

Cross-asset: government bond yields fell in US, Germany and UK while French yields rose on political and spending concerns. Oil rose sharply on attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and Hormuz tankers, gold and silver fell, the USD edged higher, and the BRL fell sharply.
Credit returned -0.55% and Arbitrage -1.01%. US IG gained on falling Treasury yields, and HY was slightly higher with lower quality underperforming.
Quant leads YTD at +12.50% and 3M at +4.14%, with Long biased YTD +10.18%.
earnings_insights: US earnings announcements toward month-end raised further questions about returns on AI investment and intensified the tech sell-off.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Second consecutive negative month after September's -0.26%, driven by the AI trade unwind.
Fed hold left the USD slightly higher and yields lower on tech-driven safe-haven demand.
Supply threats lifted commodity macro and UK energy equities.

risk_factors: Further doubts over returns on AI spending and crowded AI and tech positioning.
Middle East supply disruption affecting oil.
Brazil fiscal concerns and EM macro exposure.
Flattening yield curves and shifting rate expectations for directional macro.
vol_and_positioning: De-grossing and unwinds of crowded AI and tech trades drove multi-strategy losses across all size cohorts.
Market hedges may have offered only partial protection against volatility in AI-related positions for equity L/S.
Sharp factor rotation away from tech toward value and defensives hurt systematic equity strategies.
geopolitical: Escalating Middle East tensions, with attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, pushed oil higher.
France political and fiscal uncertainty weighed on the euro and pushed French yields higher.
Brazil's surprise election result renewed public spending concerns and hit the real.
